theory.intro: A length can be written in two ways: as a whole number of small units, or as a decimal of larger units. For example $165$ cm $= 1.65$ m.
facts: There are $100$ cm in $1$ m, so each centimetre is $\tfrac{1}{100}$ of a metre ($0.01$ m).
There are $1000$ mm in $1$ m and $10$ mm in $1$ cm.
Place value carries the meaning: $1.65$ m is $1$ whole metre and $65$ hundredths of a metre.
steps: Decide how many small units make one large unit ($100$ cm $= 1$ m).
Split the small-unit total into whole large units and a remainder.
Write the remainder as the decimal part.

foundation.question_text: Record $142$ cm as a decimal number of metres.
Interpret $3.27$ m as metres and centimetres.
Record $68$ mm as a decimal number of centimetres.
Interpret $14.6$ cm as centimetres and millimetres.
Write $5$ m $34$ cm using metres in decimal notation.
Which decimal length in metres is equivalent to $209$ cm?

development.question_text: Record $7$ cm as a decimal number of metres.
Record $9$ mm as a decimal number of metres.
Interpret $12.05$ m as metres and centimetres.
Interpret $0.7$ cm as a whole number of millimetres.
development.solution_text:
$0.7\text{ cm}=7$ tenths of a centimetre
$=7\text{ mm}$

development.question_text: Write $8$ m $4$ cm using metres in decimal notation.
Complete the equivalence: $3.\square5$ m $=3$ m $45$ cm.

mastery.question_text: Noah writes $6$ m $8$ cm as $6.8$ m. Explain his place-value error and give the correct decimal length.
mastery.solution_text:
$8\text{ cm}$ is $8$ hundredths of a metre, not $8$ tenths.
$6\text{ m }8\text{ cm}=6.08\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text:
A ribbon is $2.045$ m long.
Record its length using metres, centimetres and millimetres.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.045\text{ m}=45\text{ mm}$
$45\text{ mm}=4\text{ cm }5\text{ mm}$
$2.045\text{ m}=2\text{ m }4\text{ cm }5\text{ mm}$

mastery.question_text:
A length is written as $4.0a7$ m. It is also $4$ m $6$ cm $7$ mm.
Find the digit $a$.
mastery.solution_text:
$6\text{ cm }7\text{ mm}=67\text{ mm}=0.067\text{ m}$
$4\text{ m }6\text{ cm }7\text{ mm}=4.067\text{ m}$
$a=6$
